dataRefreshStatus.channel: Lee County Clerk of Court via FMB Chamber of Commerce
dataRefreshStatus.note: Publicly-published Lee County reports contain aggregate county totals only; Tourist Development Tax data is exempt from public records under Florida statute. FMB-specific figures require direct request through the appropriate channel.

dataRefreshStatus.metric: Residential home sales — pre-Ian (2022) monthly baselines
dataRefreshStatus.channel: RPCRA (Royal Palm Coast Realtor Association) / Lee County Property Appraiser via FMB Chamber
dataRefreshStatus.note: FMB-specific 2022 (pre-Ian) monthly closing counts are needed to compute a Sanibel-style housing recovery %. Current dashboard shows YoY direction only (Feb 2026 +69%, Dec 2025 +68%) until pre-Ian baseline is verified.

headline.label: Bed Tax Recovery (FY25 YTD vs FY22 YTD)
headline.note: FMB collected $3.85M in bed tax through August of FY25, recovering to 48% of its FY22 pre-Ian YTD baseline ($8.04M). FMB's share of the Lee County total has rebuilt from 3.45% (FY23) to 8.58% (FY25) — pre-Ian share was 12.49%.
headline.source: Lee County Clerk of Court, Tourist Development Tax breakdown by municipality, FY22–FY25 YTD through August.
headline.sourceFile: Tourist Tax Breakdown - Add'l needed - Data through August 2025.xlsx

accommodationRecovery.headline: Lodging capacity rebuilt to 66% of pre-Ian inventory
accommodationRecovery.source: Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce, Accommodations file (March 18, 2026). Hotel data as of 7/30/2025; VR data refreshed March 2026.

capacityVsRevenue.interpretation: Capacity has rebuilt faster than per-unit revenue. Each rebuilt room is generating less revenue than its pre-Ian counterpart — lower occupancy, lower rates, or both.

destroyedHotels: Carousel Inn on the Beach (27 rooms)
Outrigger Beach Resort (144, sold to London Bay)
permanentLosses.source: Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce, Accommodations file (March 18, 2026).

pipeline.headline: 877 lodging units confirmed in development across 9 projects; 2 additional projects pending plans
pipeline.verificationNote: Chamber Accommodations file dated March 18, 2026 reflects status as of mid-2025 for several projects. Status verified May 23, 2026 against Town Council/LPA records and current local reporting; nine projects updated, two reclassified to a separate Housing pipeline (residential units, not lodging), and one project (Compass Rose) marked unverified.

hotels.name: Arches Bayfront
hotels.status: Approved by Town Council June 2025 (4-1, Mayor Allers opposed); pre-construction, several years out

hotels.name: London Bay (former Outrigger / Charley's site)
hotels.status: 100 hotel rooms + 50 condo-hotel + 46 residences; LPA recommended denial May 2026; Town Council hearing June 2026

hotels.name: Lighthouse Island Resort expansion
hotels.status: Approved by Town Council June 2025 with 11 zoning deviations; expansion from 75 to 130 rooms

hotels.name: Silver Sands / TPI Hospitality
hotels.status: 5-story, 60-room hotel adjacent to Margaritaville (separate property); plans to go before Town June 2026; opening late 2028 / early 2029

hotels.name: Myerside Resort
hotels.status: Approved by Town Council June 2024 (4-1, Allers opposed); 45 hotel rooms + 4 live/work + 9,000 sf retail + 2,250 sf restaurant; construction late 2026

hotels.name: Pink Shell Bayside
hotels.status: Approved by Town Council Feb 2025 (4-0 unanimous); 6 stories, ~80 ft, bayfront

hotels.name: Times Square (Persaud)
hotels.status: Scaled from 50 to 6 boutique rooms with pool, cabanas, retail after LPA pushback; no variances needed; heading to Council

hotels.name: Wyndham
hotels.status: Pending plans — old 103-room hotel demolished after Ian damage; no rebuild plan filed; concept stage with Neighborhood Company

hotels.name: Compass Rose
hotels.status: Status unverified — Chamber file lists 'permanent holding pattern' but no public reporting confirms an active hotel project at this name

vacationRentals.name: Sea Gate / Red Coconut (Oceanside)
vacationRentals.status: Approved by Town Council Dec 2024 (3-2); residents' lawsuit dismissed by Judge McHugh May 2026; cleared to proceed. 17-story tower, 250+ ft, $52M land

vacationRentals.name: Estero Island Beach Club
vacationRentals.status: Approved May 2025 (LPA + Council unanimous); 75 multi-family timeshare units in 5-story building (reduced from 10 stories); target completion summer 2027

pipeline.source: Verified May 23, 2026 against Town Council/LPA records (fortmyersbeachfl.gov), Beach Observer, Fox 4, WINK News, Beach Talk Radio, B1039, and Gulfshore Business. Underlying inventory from Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce Accommodations file (March 18, 2026).

housingPipeline.headline: 15 residential units in development across 2 projects
housingPipeline.framing: Residential housing-for-sale projects (single-family homes and cottages), not lodging pipeline. Reclassified May 2026 from the Chamber's vacation-rental pipeline because these units are being sold as residences, not operated as short-term rentals.

projects.name: Beach Baptist Church property redevelopment
projects.status: Town Council approved phased development Oct/Nov 2025; church sold 2 acres to S.J. Collins for $4M; 12 single-family homes on Connecticut Street; church rebuild groundbreaking 6-8 months out

projects.name: Cottages of Paradise Point
projects.status: Broke ground Jan 14, 2026; 3 Gulf-front cottages (2,143 sf + 3,607 sf + 2,053 sf) starting at $2.6M; built on 15 ft concrete pilings, engineered for 160 mph winds

housingPipeline.source: Beach Observer, Fox 4, Gulfshore Business, Business Observer (Oct 2025 – Apr 2026 reporting).

sisterCityComparison.title: Lee County Bed Tax Recovery by Municipality

sisterCityComparison.source: Lee County Clerk of Court, Tourist Development Tax breakdown.

rows.note: Hit hard by Ian; recovery slower than FMB

sectors.title: Tourism & Lodging Capacity
sectors.lead: Lodging is FMB's economic engine. Pre-Ian, the town was Lee County's #1 bed-tax generator at $8.2M/year. Recovery here drives recovery everywhere else.

metrics.label: Hotel Rooms Operating
metrics.note: 1,306 hotel rooms operating across 20 properties (vs 1,724 pre-Ian). Includes the new 254-room Margaritaville Beach Resort, which opened post-Ian. At properties that existed pre-Ian, ~97% of room capacity is back online; the remaining gap is 590 rooms at destroyed properties.
metrics.source: Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce, Accommodations file (March 18, 2026). Hotel data as of 7/30/2025.
metrics.trendLabel: Stronger than the Google-Places business database alone suggests

metrics.label: Hotel Properties Operating
metrics.note: 20 of 40 pre-Ian hotel properties are operating. 17 properties were permanently destroyed (590 rooms lost); 3 remain temporarily closed (Beach Shell Inn, Manatee Bay Inn, Tahitian Inn). Property-count recovery lags room-count recovery because surviving properties have larger room counts on average.
metrics.source: Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce, Accommodations file (March 18, 2026).
metrics.trendLabel: 17 properties permanently lost; 3 still working toward reopening

metrics.label: Vacation Rental Rooms Operating
metrics.note: 2,853 vacation rental rooms operating across ~60 properties (vs 4,539 pre-Ian). The Chamber's room-based count is more comparable to hotel rooms than the license-based count from the FMB business database (1,982 active + 160 delinquent licenses). 624 VR rooms remain in temporarily-closed properties; 226 rooms permanently destroyed.
metrics.source: Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce, Accommodations file (March 18, 2026). VR numbers refreshed March 2026.
metrics.trendLabel: VR-led recovery is FMB's distinctive pattern

metrics.label: Delinquent VR Licenses (Likely Offline)
metrics.note: 160 vacation rental licenses are delinquent — properties unable to operate. 7.5% of 2,142 total licenses (1,982 active + 160 delinquent).
metrics.trendLabel: Leading indicator — these properties have not returned to operation

metrics.label: Tourist Attractions Operating
metrics.note: 32 of 33 tracked tourist attractions operational. 1 temporarily closed.

metrics.label: Bed Tax Recovery (YTD)
metrics.note: FMB collected $3.85M through August of FY25 — 48% of its $8.04M pre-Ian baseline. Curve: 15% → 37% → 48%. FMB share of Lee County total: 8.58% (was 12.49% pre-Ian, #1 municipal contributor).
metrics.source: Lee County Clerk of Court, Tourist Development Tax breakdown by municipality.
metrics.sourceFile: Tourist Tax Breakdown - Add'l needed - Data through August 2025.xlsx

sectors.title: Lodging Mix Shift
sectors.lead: FMB's recovery is structurally different from Sanibel's. Hotels were heavily destroyed; vacation rentals rebuilt faster. The result is a town economically more dependent on short-term rentals than ever before.

metrics.label: Hotel Rooms vs VR Licenses (Current)
metrics.note: 754 hotel rooms vs 1,982 active VR licenses. VR-led ratio: 2.6× — far more skewed toward short-term rentals than pre-Ian mix.
metrics.trendLabel: Structural shift away from hotel-led lodging

sectors.title: Economic Activity
sectors.lead: Beyond lodging, FMB's economy runs on restaurants, retail, and services tied to tourism volume. These metrics measure whether the daytime economy has returned.

metrics.label: Restaurants Operating
metrics.note: 47 of approximately 70 pre-Ian restaurants. Includes restaurants categorized as 'Restaurant' in the business database; bars and cafés counted separately.
metrics.source: Baseline: pre-Ian TripAdvisor restaurant rankings (~70 listed). Current: fmb-baseline-report-march-2026.xlsx Restaurants & Dining sheet.
metrics.trendLabel: Pre-Ian baseline approximate — Town of FMB business license records would refine

metrics.label: Total Businesses Operational
metrics.note: 294 currently operational of 299 tracked. Pre-Ian baseline pending — Town of FMB business tax receipts.

metrics.label: Marinas
metrics.note: 22 marinas operating. Critical to FMB's fishing, charter, and recreational tourism. Baseline pending.

metrics.label: Real Estate Offices
metrics.note: 40 real estate offices — high count reflects active sales / rebuild market. Not a pure recovery indicator (compare Sanibel's exclusion of listings).

sectors.title: Watchlist — Leading Indicators
sectors.lead: Headline counts can mask trouble. These are the signals to watch quarter-over-quarter for early warning that recovery is stalling.

metrics.label: Café Closure Concentration
metrics.note: 3 of 7 cafés temporarily closed — 43% closure rate. Cafés have marginal economics and reopen last when foot traffic is slow to return. Highest closure rate of any category.
metrics.trendLabel: Concentrated risk — watch for further closures or reopenings

metrics.label: Currently Closed Businesses
metrics.note: 5 businesses temporarily closed: 3 cafés, 1 tourist attraction, 1 service business. 0 permanently closed (any business that fully closed would not appear in this dataset).
metrics.trendLabel: Small denominator — the 160 delinquent VR licenses are a larger risk signal

metrics.label: Population
metrics.note: 5,513 residents (2024 ACS estimate) vs 5,582 at 2020 Census. Surface number looks flat, but US Census Bureau ACS reports a -21.8% change 2019-2024, suggesting fluctuation around displacement and partial return.
metrics.source: US Census Bureau Quick Facts; American Community Survey 2024 estimates.
metrics.trendLabel: Population is context, not a recovery metric per se

housingMarket.headline: Home sales recovering — pre-Ian baseline pending
housingMarket.framing: Activity / direction indicator. Sanibel-style recovery % requires pre-Ian (2022) monthly closings baseline, currently being requested from RPCRA / Lee County Property Appraiser.

metrics.label: Home Sales — most recent month (YoY)
metrics.confirmingDataPoint: December 2025 (37 closings) vs December 2024 (22) = +68% — same direction
metrics.note: 44 homes sold in February 2026 vs 26 in February 2025 — +69% YoY. December 2025 confirms (+68% over Dec 2024). Sales volume is rising as rebuilt homes and condos come online.

sources.source: Redfin Fort Myers Beach housing market data

metrics.label: Median Price + Days on Market (context)
metrics.note: Median price $580K (−30.7% YoY) reflects a mix shift toward smaller rebuilt properties, not a market collapse. Days-on-market 134 (up from 91) indicates a buyer's market.
metrics.source: Redfin Fort Myers Beach housing market data, February 2026.

rebuildingActivity.headline: Rebuild surge winding down; recovery funding tapering
rebuildingActivity.framing: Context only — not included in any composite recovery percentage. Per Sanibel methodology, permit and disaster-fund activity measures reconstruction surge, not return to normalcy. Both signal sets here are expected to decline as recovery progresses.

rebuildSignals.label: Building Fund Revenue (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
rebuildSignals.note: Permit-fund revenue projected down 29.6% in FY26 — the cleanest signal that the post-Ian rebuilding surge is past peak.
rebuildSignals.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget, All Fund Revenues.

rebuildSignals.label: Summer Permit Volume (Jun–Aug YoY)
rebuildSignals.note: Monthly summer permit counts dropped from 109/151/145 (Jun-Aug 2024) to 89/99/101 (Jun-Aug 2025) — a 29% YoY decline in volume that mirrors the Building Fund revenue drop from a different source.
rebuildSignals.source: FMB Chamber of Commerce, Permits sheet (Accommodations file, March 2026).

rebuildSignals.label: Code Enforcement Fees (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
rebuildSignals.note: Code enforcement activity projected down 50% — fewer post-Ian compliance issues as properties return to standard operation.
rebuildSignals.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget, Revenues Line Item Detail.

fiscalContext.label: Half-Cent Sales Tax (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
fiscalContext.note: Half-cent sales tax projected down 37% — population displacement and slower commercial activity flowing through to the general fund.
fiscalContext.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget.

fiscalContext.label: Emergency Fund / Disaster Reimbursements (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
fiscalContext.note: Federal disaster reimbursements projected down 83% — the recovery-funding tap is closing as Ian's eligible reimbursement window expires.
fiscalContext.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget, All Fund Revenues.

fiscalContext.label: FDEM Hurricane Recovery Funds (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
fiscalContext.note: State recovery funds essentially flat at $4.7M — still flowing, but no longer growing. The next budget cycle will likely see this number drop substantially as project-specific allocations close out.
fiscalContext.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget, All Fund Revenues.

pendingBaselines: Vacation rental licenses (pre-Ian) — Lee County Tax Collector records
Total business count (pre-Ian) — Town of FMB business tax receipt records
Restaurant count (pre-Ian) — refine ~70 estimate with Town of FMB or FMB Chamber data
Residential home sales (pre-Ian, monthly 2022) — RPCRA / Lee County Property Appraiser
FMB-specific FY26 Q1 bed tax (Oct-Dec 2025) — Lee County Clerk of Court via FMB Chamber
Restaurants & Dining detail sheet baselines (per-restaurant pre-Ian status)

rules: Compare current value to pre-Ian baseline where available
Cap recovery percentage at 100% (exceeding baseline counts as fully recovered)
Mark 'baseline pending' rather than fabricate when data is unverified
Exclude inverse indicators (e.g., real estate listings — high inventory signals distress)
Surface leading indicators (delinquent VR licenses, café closures) as watchlist, not headline
